name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=cursor/camera). Descriptor accurately captures the behavior: pans the cursor AND the viewport window together. No Ghidra address residue in the name. Consistent with sibling pan functions in the same file (fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated, fd2_pan_cursor_to_char).
purpose: Animated camera pan that scrolls the battle viewport window and the cursor together (one tile per frame) until the window origin reaches the caller-supplied target tile position.
logic_summary: Resets data_fd2_battle_anim_phase to 0. Pans X first: while view_window_origin_x != target_ox, step both cursor_world_x and view_window_origin_x by -1 (target below current) or +1 (target above/equal), then call fd2_composite_battle_frame(0) and fd2_clear_keyboard_buffer() each iteration. Then pans Y identically with cursor_world_y / view_window_origin_y vs target_oy. Because cursor world coord and window origin move by the same delta each step, the cursor stays at the same on-screen position while the world scrolls beneath it. Comparisons are signed (int). __CHK(0x14) is the Watcom stack-probe prologue (not game logic).

params.name: target_ox
params.semantics: Target X tile column for the viewport window origin (left edge). Callers pass small literal tile columns (e.g. 0, 3, 4, 5). Loop pans view_window_origin_x to this value.
params.reason: Accurate and unambiguous abbreviation (o = origin); not generic (not param_N), no address residue. Documented in the comment as the target window origin X.

params.name: target_oy
params.semantics: Target Y tile row for the viewport window origin (top edge). Callers pass tile rows (e.g. 0, 0xC, 0xF, 0x22, 0x2A, 0x2B for tall prologue maps). Loop pans view_window_origin_y to this value.
params.reason: Accurate and unambiguous abbreviation (o = origin); not generic, no address residue. Documented in the comment as the target window origin Y.

returns.semantics: No return value; effect is the animated scroll plus updated window-origin and cursor-world globals.
